entries.proposition: Ethosuximide abolished spontaneous spike-wave discharges in these mutant-model mice, while baclofen worsened them; the ethosuximide arm is within-animal before and after in four mice with no wild-type or vehicle arm described, since control mice do not have the discharges.
entries.snippet: Ethosuximide had an acute effect on the frequency of SWDs and abolished SWDs 30 min after treatment (Fig. 4C and E).
entries.anchor: Results, PV-ArchT mice displayed an absence seizure phenotype

entries.proposition: The measured T-type current is LOWER, not higher, in the model's reticular-nucleus PV neurons: peak T-current about 155 pA against about 699 pA in control and rebound bursts impaired, with three mice per group as the statistical unit.
entries.snippet: ArchT-expressing TRN PV cells possessed significantly lower peak current than controls (Fig. 6F) (155 ± 68 pA for PV-ArchT versus 699 ± 36 pA for controls, t4 = −7, P = 0.006: Fig. 6G).
entries.anchor: Results, ArchT expression impaired hyperpolarization-induced rebound excitation in TRN PV-positive neurons

entries.proposition: The authors face the tension themselves: T-current is impaired, yet ethosuximide works; they look for T-type mRNA upregulation and find none, and say that alterations in mRNA do not account for the ethosuximide-sensitive component, so the efficacy of ethosuximide here is not explained by a measured T-type gain. Their abstract's phrase 'suggesting a gain of function of T-type calcium channels' is an inference not supported by the measured current or the transcript data.
entries.snippet: These negative data indicate that alterations in Cav mRNA expression levels could not account for the ethosuximide-sensitive component of cortical and thalamic hyperactivity.
entries.anchor: Results, Thalamic hyperactivity was synchronized to cortical SWDs in PV-ArchT mice

entries.proposition: The authors cite that in Cav3.2 and Cav3.3 double knockout mice, in which TRN rebound bursts are abolished, gamma-butyrolactone-induced discharges still occur and remain highly sensitive to ethosuximide (a second line of evidence that ethosuximide efficacy does not require the TRN T-type rebound mechanism). This is cited, not read here; the primary is parked (restricted deposit).
entries.snippet: Moreover, GBL-induced SWDs were highly sensitive to the T-type Ca2+ channel blocker, ethosuximide.35
entries.anchor: Discussion, Do cortical SWDs require the rebound excitation of TRN PV-positive neurons?

entries.proposition: The model rests on an opsin's cell-type toxicity, not on a human-genotype lesion: the authors say ArchT expressed without light caused abnormal waves and had a toxic effect on PV cells, and that the phenotype regressed when expression was switched off. Face and predictive validity are claimed from discharges plus ethosuximide response.
entries.snippet: indicating that ArchT expression—even without light activation—had a toxic effect on PV-positive cells.
entries.anchor: Results, PV-ArchT mice displayed an absence seizure phenotype

entries.proposition: Figure 6 read as an image (page 12 raster): rebound bursts per cell about 2.2 in controls (three mice) versus about 1.0 in PV-ArchT (three mice), star; T-current peak about 700 pA versus about 155 pA, three stars with the per-mouse points of about 700 to 750 against about 40 to 275; Figure 4E: ethosuximide before about 23 events per hour (range about 8 to 50) falling to about 1 (four mice), baclofen about 33 rising to about 63.
